text:
**The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a good fit: it has a **2,600 W AC inverter** and **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity, so it can handle a single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, with some power headroom. [Product details and buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)

At full cooktop power, expect roughly **about an hour of continuous use** from a 2,000 Wh-class station; actual cooking time varies with heat setting and cycling. [Runtime estimates](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop)

An electric kettle should work too **if its wattage is below the station’s 2,600 W continuous output**—check the label on your kettle before buying.
